newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK Jan industrial production data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK Jan industrial production data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK data showing January manufacturing output up 0.3 percent m/m and 1.6 percent y/y and overall industrial production unchanged m/m and up 2.4 percent y/y.

"No surprises whatsoever...Two things worth noting -- the purchasing managers index signalled that manufacturing output would rise while the CBI expectation survey signalled that in the months ahead we may well see a slowdown in already subdued growth in manufacturing output."

"They are certainly consistent with the picture that manufacturing is going below trend at the turn of the year. We've seen signs that retailers' orders to manufacturers started to slow and with sterling having remained fairly robust, that is going to affect export orders as well. I think the picture is for continued sluggish growth at best and we may well veer back towards a period of no growth at all in manufacturing."

"The data are very supportive for the Chancellor yet again. The Bank of England's argument would be that it is the service sector which has been driving growth higher, but really the signs are that it is the consumer slowdown that is going to start feeding through into that area. If you have manufacturing growing below trend, the service sector slowing from an above-trend rate to trend, perhaps, then...the justification for rate increases looks pretty weak."

"Manufacturing output rose a much as expected 0.3 percent in January. Annual growth stands at 1.6 pecent, confirming that the positive GDP profile remains lopsided and heavily weighted towards services. Data will in part reflect stg strength but overall gain also in line with the bulk of the inventory correction process having been undertaken. Total industrial production was hit by the weather and a flat reading here should not be seen as indicative of the underlying picture. Data should have little impact. Indeed moderate growth combined with what should be very good inflation data near term make for a positive backdrop to gilts and short sterling."
